headline: Over 70 Dogs Rescued from South Korean Farm as Nation Bans Dog Meat
meta_description: More than 70 dogs rescued from a South Korean dog meat farm ahead of the country's nationwide ban on dog meat taking full effect in February 2027.
summary_short: More than 70 dogs have been rescued from a South Korean dog meat farm in what may be the country's final large-scale rescue before a nationwide ban takes effect.
body:
More than 70 dogs have been rescued from a South Korean dog meat farm in what may represent the country's final large-scale rescue of its kind. The operation comes as South Korea moves toward a nationwide ban on dog meat consumption, set to take full effect in February 2027.

The rescue marks a significant moment in the country's ongoing shift away from the practice. With a legal ban now set to become fully enforceable within months, fewer such operations are expected to remain. The timing underscores how far attitudes have shifted within a single generation—from widespread acceptance to legislative prohibition.

For the 70 dogs involved, the rescue represents a second chance at life, away from the conditions of a farm system that is rapidly becoming illegal across the nation.
quick_facts: More than 70 dogs rescued from South Korean dog meat farm
Nationwide ban on dog meat takes full effect February 2027
Rescue may be country's final large-scale operation of its kind
